opps.body: Sales are down 581 cases (34%) vs last year, but Famosa is still 10.7% of your total commission — your #3 brand. That decline has already cost about $581 in modeled commission, and recovering half of it is worth roughly $290. On a brand this size that is a bigger swing than anything you could realistically open new this year. 27 accounts bought it last year; 25 have this year — 2 accounts stopped carrying it.

opps.title: 4 accounts stopped ordering — $194 of commission gone quiet
opps.body: Each of these bought from you last year and has ordered nothing at all in 2026. A lost account is the most expensive kind of decline: there is no brand mix to fix and nothing replaces it automatically — the whole relationship has stopped. The largest, American Legion Post 60 Roselle Park, was worth 103 cases last year on its own. These are the calls with the shortest path back to commission, because the account already knows you.

opps.title: 5 accounts holding all year but soft this month — 101 cases behind
opps.body: Year to date each of these is fine, so the relationship is not the problem — but month to date they are all well behind where they were last August. That is the pattern that becomes a bad quarter if nobody catches it, and it is the cheapest kind to fix: the account is still buying, it just has not placed its usual order yet. Together they are 101 cases and about $101 of commission behind last August's pace, with days left in the month to close it.

opps.title: Colt 45 alone is 24% of your commission
opps.body: Your top brand carries 24% of your commission and your top three carry 50%. That concentration cuts both ways: a single point move in Colt 45 is worth more to you than anything else on your board, so it deserves first call every week — and a supplier change or a lost placement there would hit harder than anywhere else in your book.

opps.title: Sapporo — growing 26% while your book is -22%
opps.body: Sapporo is up 335 cases (26%) YoY against a portfolio that is -22%. It is running 47 points ahead of your book and is currently in 42 of your 63 active accounts. This is where a placement lands easiest — the brand is already proving itself in your territory, and it has added about $335 in modeled commission so far.

opps.title: 4 brands with real placement gaps — 42 open doors
opps.body: These brands land in far more accounts like yours than they do in your book. The comparison is not raw company share: it weights each brand's on- and off-premise placement rate by your own channel mix, so an on-premise book is never judged against a supermarket brand's reach. Each door below is valued at what a typical account doing business in that brand actually buys company-wide (the median, not an average), scaled down to the size of the doors you actually call on — so these are ordinary placements in YOUR kind of account, not best-case ones in someone else's. Closing every gap would be worth roughly $230 — that is a ceiling, not a forecast, and it compares against $10,697 of commission in your book today. Take the top one or two lines; the whole list is not a year's work.
